state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think the transformation is a translation by a vector of \(\left[\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 3 \end{array}\right]\)? Can you explain how you arrived at that conclusion?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought that since the \(x\) value is changing to \(x-3\), it means the graph moves up by 3 units. I guess I got confused because I thought it was like moving the whole graph up instead of sideways. So, does that mean it actually moves to the right instead?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think the function \(f(x - a)\) moves the graph to the right instead of up? Can you think of a way to test this hypothesis with a specific example?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively engages the misconception through questioning, maintains high cognitive demand by asking for testing with examples, and the student shows clear progress from thinking the graph moves up to recognizing it moves right, though final understanding isn't fully confirmed.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking, never provides the answer directly, and in Turn 3 suggests using a specific example to test the student's reasoning—all hallmarks of the Socratic method.
